metadata.title: Prerequisite-Conditioned Causal Continuation Gating in a Language Model
metadata.description: This preprint reports behavioral qualification and causal analysis of PCCG-Qwen3-4B, a Qwen3-4B-derived open-weight model trained to condition continuation on fixed-width four-digit equality. With thinking enabled, the model generates a four-bit digit-comparison trace, closes the reasoning frame, and selects either GO followed by native end-of-sequence (EOS) for equal operands or immediate native EOS for unequal operands, with zero final-answer payload. The fused checkpoint produces the exact required token sequence on 4,096/4,096 recorded conditions, including 1,024/1,024 cases in a separate final set. Evaluation uses full-vocabulary greedy decoding without forced termination, an external truth gate, or output rewriting. Anthropic’s Jacobian Lens is fitted on 16 generated reasoning prefixes at transformer blocks 24 through 29 to measure intermediate GO/EOS preferences. A fixed 2,560-dimensional activation-difference direction is estimated separately, with its intervention block and strength selected on development data and frozen before confirmation. On 40 fresh matched pairs, the block-29 intervention reverses GO to immediate EOS on 40/40 equal cases and EOS to GO followed by EOS on 40/40 unequal cases. All 640 control outputs remain unchanged across eight controls applied to the same 80 contexts. Prompt tokens, model weights, and the normally generated correct reasoning prefix are held fixed during each replayed intervention. Fused weights, tokenizer, training provenance, evaluation cases, raw token and logit records, fitted Jacobian matrices, intervention artifacts, and reproduction code are released at immutable repository commits. The findings establish a causally sufficient internal continuation-control direction under the tested equality policy: the correct reasoning prefix remains fixed while the subsequent native continuation decision is reversed.

title: Prerequisite-Conditioned Causal Continuation Gating in a Language Model
